title: Core language
goal: `vex run hello.vx` compiles and runs native programs with structs, lists, methods and string interpolation.

tasks.text: Repo layout, `go.mod`, `.gitignore`, git init
`vex` CLI skeleton: `version`, `help`; `run`, `build`, `emit-c` added with V-045
Error type with file:line:col, a source snippet, a caret and an optional hint
Tokens: identifiers, keywords, int/float/string/bool literals, operators
Automatic statement end at newline (Go-style rules)
Comments `//`, `///` and `/* */`, string escapes, `1_000` digit separators
String interpolation tokens: `"Hi {name}, {count + 1}"` with nesting
Lexer unit tests
AST node types for declarations, statements and expressions
Top level: `fn`, `struct` with fields, default values, methods and `static fn`
Functions: typed parameters, default values, `-> Type`, one-line `=> expr` bodies
Statements: `let`, `var`, assignment and `+= -= *= /= %=`, `if/else if/else` without parentheses, `while`, `return`, `break`, `continue`
Loops: `for x in list`, `for i, x in list`, `for i in a..b`, `for i in a..=b`
Expressions with a Pratt parser: precedence, unary, call, index, member access, list literals `[1, 2]`
Call syntax shared by functions, constructors and future widgets: positional plus named arguments `User(name: "Ann")`, trailing blocks `f(x) { ... }`
Helpful messages for common mistakes, e.g. `else` on a new line, `;` or `()` around `if` conditions
Parser unit tests
Types: `int`, `float`, `bool`, `string`, `[T]` lists, structs
Scopes, name resolution, shadowing rules
Type inference for `let x = ...`; annotation for empty lists (`let xs: [int] = []`)
`let` (immutable) vs `var` (mutable) enforcement
Named and default arguments: matching, missing or unknown names, duplicates
Structs: constructor `User(...)` from fields, field defaults, methods with implicit `self` (fields used without `self.`), `static fn` called as `User.guest()`
Missing-return detection on all paths
Built-in functions: `print`, `println`, `input`, `panic`, `assert`, `int()`, `float()`, `str()`
Built-in members: lists `.len`, `.push()`, `.pop()`, `.contains()`; strings `.len`, `.upper()`, `.lower()`, `.contains()`, `.split()`
Clear type errors with hints, e.g. int + string suggests `"{count} items"`, int/float mix suggests `float()`
C runtime: lists, strings, allocation, printing
Runtime safety: bounds checks, divide by zero, bad number parsing, empty `pop()`, all with file and line
Codegen: functions, defaults, named arguments, structs, methods, all statements and expressions
String interpolation codegen for every printable type
Printing lists and structs: `[1, 2]`, `User(name: "Ann", age: 30)`
Call clang with `-fwrapv -O2`; respect the `$CC` environment variable
Golden tests: `examples/*.vx` + `*.out`, run by `go test`
Error tests: `tests/errors/*.vx` with an expected message
Examples: hello, fibonacci, structs/methods, prime sieve, sorting, input
`README.md`: install, CLI, language tour

title: Language for apps
goal: wrapping a large C library is mostly generated, not written by hand, and the native packages for the UI framework (Firebase, payments, maps) can be built on it. New syntax in these tasks is approved before it is built.

tasks.text: Enums with data plus `match` (exhaustive)
Optionals `User?` with `if let`, `??` and `?.`; no null crashes
Errors: `throws` / `throws(E)`, `throw`, `try`, `catch`, `try?`
Closures / lambdas, needed for UI event handlers
Generics for functions and structs
Maps `[string: int]`
Interfaces: a struct declares which interfaces it implements
Modules: a folder is a module; `import "vex:math"`, `import "models"`, `as`; `pub` visibility; `package.toml`; first `vex:math` and `vex:strings`
Memory management: tracing GC, stage 1 mark and sweep
Hardening: fuzzing, sanitizers, Linux and macOS CI, feature-combination tests
Hardening 2: random program generator with known output, stack overflow errors, independent review
Integer overflow stops the program by default; `&+` `&-` `&*` wrap; benchmarked against Go
C interop: `extern fn` with `as "c_name"`, string conversion, `[c]` sources, libs and flags in `package.toml`
Standard library: float math in `vex:math` through C (`sqrt`, `sin`, …) and `vex:time`
Standard library: files, processes and environment (`vex:fs`, `vex:os`); `vex run` passes arguments
Strings: `replace`, `trim`, `trimStart`, `trimEnd`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `indexOf`, `substring`, `chars`, `lines`
Standard library: strings, math, time and files, delivered by V-127, V-129 and V-131
Builder blocks: a trailing `{ }` for a list parameter builds the list, one element per line, with `let`, `if`, `for` and `...`; `Column { }` without `()`
Collection `if`, `for` and spread `...`/`...?` inside list and map literals, as in Dart
Setters `set name(v: T)` and `didSet` blocks on fields with `oldValue`
Getters `get name -> T`, read like fields
Generics: generic enums such as `Result<T>`, methods with their own type parameters, generic functions as values (`first<int>` or from the expected type)
Interfaces: generic interfaces such as `Ordered<T>`, interfaces that extend others, enums that implement interfaces, getters and setters in interfaces, met by accessors or fields

C interop: sized numbers (`int32`, `uint8`, `float32`...) in extern signatures, `extern type` pointer handles, `fn` callbacks with a kept context, `export fn`, Objective-C `.m` sources and Apple frameworks

sections.title: Needed by the UI framework (Phase 3 starts after these)

tasks.text: `async`/`await` with an event loop: `async fn`, `Future<T>`, `await`, `all`/`any`, `run`, `time.sleep`, and `vex_poll` for platform run loops; each task runs on its own stack
Streams: `Stream<T>`, `async fn ... -> Stream<T>` with `yield`, `for await`, and `StreamController<T>`, for UI events and HTTP bodies
Isolates: `isolate.run` and `isolate.spawn` run code in parallel on threads with their own heaps; `Channel<T>` carries deep-copied messages between them; `while let`
Bitwise operators `& | ^ ~ << >>` and `&= |= ^= <<= >>=` on `int`, with `&` binding tighter than `==`; shifts outside 0–63 stop the program

List essentials: `sort()`, `sort(by:)`, `sorted`, `reversed`, `insert(x, at:)`, `remove(at:)`, `removeWhere`, `indexOf`, `first`, `last`, `isEmpty`, `find`, `any`, `all`, `reduce`, `join`, `flatMap`, `clear`, `min`, `max`, `sum`, `slice`; sorting is stable

Safe parsing and number basics: `int.parse(s)` and `float.parse(s)` returning optionals, `int.parse(s, radix: 16)`, `int.max`/`int.min`, `float.infinity`/`float.nan`, `isNaN`/`isFinite`, `toFixed`, `str(n, radix:)`
Conditional values: `if … else …` as an expression, with `else` required
Type tests on interface values: `x is T`, `x as? T`, and type patterns in `match` and `if case` for any interface; shares the pattern work with V-144

Equality and hashing: synthesised `Equatable`/`Hashable` for structs and enums, hand-written `hash()`, structs, records and enums as map keys, `==` on lists and maps of Equatable values, `===` for identity
Top-level and `static` `var`/`let`, initialised lazily, one copy per isolate
Async everywhere: async closures, async function values, async interface methods and async tear-offs; extends the closure part of V-148
Cancellation and timeouts: `future.cancel()`, cancellation reaching `await` points as an error, `time.timeout(future, ms)`, task groups that cancel their children
Platform conditionals: `os.target` and `os.arch` as compile-time constants whose dead branches are skipped, and per-target `[c]` sources in `package.toml`
Records in the Dart 3 style: `(int, string)`, `({int x, int y})`, `.$1` and named fields, value equality, and `let`/`var`/`for` destructuring
Destructuring and richer patterns: `let (a, b) = pair`, struct and list patterns, guards in `match` arms, ranges, `if case`
Constants: top-level `const` values computed at compile time
Extensions: add methods to existing types, built-in ones included
Type aliases for long types
Multi-line and raw strings
Operator overloading for structs: arithmetic, `==`, ordering and indexing
Tear-offs: methods and constructors as values, as in `names.map(user.greet)`
Sealed interfaces: a closed set of structs that `match` checks exhaustively, with type patterns
Null-aware elements in collections and `?[ ]` indexing
Extension types: zero-cost wrappers that make `UserId` and `int` different types
Trailing blocks with parameters: `xs.map { x in x * 2 }`, and an implicit name for a single parameter
Fields: `let` fields set once at creation, field types inferred from defaults, `init` blocks for validation, a generated `copy(field:)`, fields readable everywhere but set only inside the type
Optional ergonomics: `if let x` shorthand, comma-separated conditions in `if`/`while`/`guard`, `guard cond else`, and `?? return`/`throw`/`break`/`continue`
Control flow: `defer`, labelled `break`/`continue`, `repeat { } while`
Ranges as values: a `Range` type with `contains`, `step` and `reversed`, and list slicing `xs[1..3]`
Iteration: an `Iterable<T>` interface that `for in` accepts, and generators with `yield`; shares machinery with V-148
Enum reflection: `Type.cases`, `.name`, raw values `enum C: int { red = 1 }` with `C(rawValue:)` returning an optional, `==` on enums with data, operators on enums
Interfaces: static requirements, `Self`, generic methods and extensions of interfaces; needed for typed JSON (V-109)
Custom printing: a `toString()` method used by `println`, `str` and interpolation
Local named functions, recursive ones included
List conversion between element types: `[B]` passed as `[A]` for a fresh copy, and `cast<A>()`
Package manager: `vex get` from public git repos, `package.lock` with hashes
`vex doc`: API docs from `///` comments
Benchmark suite in the repo (`bench/`): Vex programs with Go equivalents and a script that compares them
Stack traces: runtime errors list the chain of calls with their lines
Modules, next steps: warn about unused imports, `pub` names whose types are private, and errors sorted with the root module first
`vex test`: test blocks or `_test.vx` files, filtering by name, and failures that show both values
Build modes: `--debug` (`-O0 -g`, keeps the C) and `--sanitize=address,undefined` alongside today's `-O3`, and `$VEX_CFLAGS` documented in `vex help build`
Warnings for unused local variables and unreachable code, and diagnostics that name unsupported features (`is`, labels, `defer`, `x!`)
Docs fixes: stale lines about properties, tear-offs and `==` in SYNTAX.md, typed fields in the UI sketch, and the conditional-value, overloading and inheritance decisions in the log
JSON encode/decode built in, no codegen step
Bytes: a type for binary data, and reading and writing binary files
Print values through one growing buffer; deeply nested values print in quadratic time today
Unicode-aware strings: `upper`/`lower` beyond A–Z, and counting visible characters (grapheme clusters)
GC stage 2: precise roots and object layouts
GC stage 3: generational collection (done), returning memory to the OS
Leave out the overflow and bounds checks the compiler proves can't fail, and the capacity check of presized list fills
`Set<T>` of Hashable values, with literals, `insert`, `remove`, `contains`, `union`, `intersection` and `subtracting`
Map helpers: `isEmpty`, `getOrPut`, `update`, `filter`, `mapValues`, `entries`
String helpers: `isEmpty`, `lastIndexOf`, `count`, a `split` limit, `padStart`/`padEnd`, `reversed`, `capitalize`, and `vex:strings` functions as methods
Format specs in interpolation: `"{x:.2}"`, `"{n:04}"`, `"{n:x}"`
Standard library: `vex:random`, `vex:datetime` (`now`, `Duration`, ISO 8601, calendar fields), `eprintln` and `os.stderr`, and `vex:regex`

`vex:crypto`: SHA-2, HMAC, HKDF, secure random bytes, UUID v4, constant-time compare, Argon2id and PBKDF2, `seal`/`open` with ChaCha20-Poly1305 or AES-256-GCM, Ed25519 and P-256 signatures. Only audited code (Monocypher) or each system's provider (CryptoKit, Conscrypt, CNG, libcrypto), never our own primitives; keys are their own types; MD5 and SHA-1 only under `legacy`; RFC and Wycheproof test vectors in CI on every system
`vex` on Windows: paths, temporary folders, finding clang, `.exe` outputs, `run`, `build`, `test`, `doc` and `get`, and CRLF source files
Runtime threads on Windows: isolates, channels and thread-local storage on Win32
Async tasks and generators on Windows: switching stacks allocated with `VirtualAlloc`, with guard pages
Collector on Windows: heap memory from `VirtualAlloc`, thread stack bounds and saved registers for root scanning
Standard library on Windows: `vex:fs`, `vex:os` (arguments, environment, exit codes, console UTF-8), time, `vex:datetime` local offsets, and `BCryptGenRandom` for random seeds
Windows CI: every PR runs the suite and the sanitizer-free battery on `windows-latest`

SDK archives for Windows, Linux and macOS: `vex`, the standard library, runtime, docs and the C toolchain wherever its license allows (LLVM-MinGW on Windows, clang with a musl sysroot on Linux; macOS uses the Xcode Command Line Tools). The layout is relocatable, finding everything next to the `vex` binary, so the UI framework's archive can embed it as Flutter's embeds Dart. Release CI builds, signs and checksums them, and tests each archive on a clean machine; a `winget` package points at the Windows one
`vex doctor`: checks the toolchain and, for app builds, Xcode and Android Studio with its SDK and NDK, saying what is missing and how to install it; it never installs those itself
`extern struct`: C structs passed and returned by value in extern calls, with C field layout, nested structs and fixed-size arrays
C memory: a pointer type for C-owned buffers with typed reads and writes, `Bytes` passed to C as a pointer and length without a copy, and C strings borrowed or adopted without a copy
Releasing C resources: an `extern type` can name its release function, so the collector frees unreachable handles, alongside explicit `close()` with `defer`
C enums, unions, bitfields and `#define` constants
Variadic C functions such as `printf` and `open`, using C's default argument promotions
Callbacks, next steps: struct, `Bytes` and pointer parameters, and callbacks that C calls from its own threads, queued onto the isolate that owns them
`vex bind c`: generates Vex declarations from C headers through clang's AST, filtered by name prefix, and a `bind` entry in the `[c]` section of `package.toml` that regenerates them on build
C interop guide with worked SQLite and libcurl wrappers, built and run in CI

title: Developer experience
goal: editor support and a debugger on par with Flutter's. Tools that inspect running UI apps, such as DevTools, belong to the UI framework in the `vex-ui` repo.

tasks.text: Hot reload on the simulator: reload code as a dynamic library, keep state
Language server, `vex lsp`: errors as you type, hover, go-to-definition, find references, rename, autocomplete, signature help and quick fixes from the compiler's hints, for every editor
`vex fmt` code formatter
`vex new myapp` project template
`vex repl`: type a line, see its result (compiled behind the scenes)
Debugging: line info in the generated C (`#line`) so lldb shows `.vx` lines
Debug adapter, `vex dap`: breakpoints, stepping, call stacks and variables shown as Vex values over lldb, for any editor that speaks the Debug Adapter Protocol
VS Code extension: highlighting, snippets, the language server, formatting on save, run and debug buttons, tasks for `vex build`, `run` and `test`, and a test explorer
JetBrains plugin for IntelliJ IDEA, Android Studio, CLion and the other JetBrains IDEs: highlighting, live templates, the language server, run configurations, the debugger and a test runner
Snippets shared by both plugins: `struct`, `enum`, `interface`, `match`, `test`, `async fn` and the like
Device picker in both plugins: choose the Mac, a simulator, an emulator or a phone, then run and hot reload from the editor
Publish the plugins to the VS Code Marketplace, Open VSX and the JetBrains Marketplace

title: Devices and IoT
goal: Vex programs on single-board computers such as the Raspberry Pi, talking to sensors and networks, then a first program on a microcontroller. Builds on the C interop steps (V-188 to V-195). New syntax in these tasks is approved before it is built.

tasks.text: Cross builds: `vex build --target linux-arm64` and `linux-armv7` from any host, using the SDK's clang and musl
Async tasks and generators on 32-bit ARM: the stack switch for armv7, with the collector's register scan
SDK archive for Linux arm64, tested on a Raspberry Pi in CI
`vex:gpio`: digital pins, edge events as streams, and PWM through the Linux character device
I²C, SPI and serial ports in the standard library or first-party packages
MQTT client package with TLS, reconnects and a stream of messages
`vex deploy`: copy a build to a board over SSH and run it, streaming its output
Spike: a freestanding runtime (no OS, no threads, a fixed heap set at build time) that blinks an LED and reads a sensor on an RP2040 or ESP32-C3; measures flash and RAM use and decides the next tasks
Memory-mapped registers and interrupt handlers, if the spike shows the runtime fits
`vex flash` and a serial monitor for supported boards
